parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The supplied circuit and graph show terminal potential difference V against current I for a cell. (a) Determine the emf ε and internal resistance r. (b) An identical cell is added in series and the voltmeter is placed across both cells. Describe how the new V–I graph differs.

answer.text: Official markscheme results: ε=1.50 V, r=0.75 Ω; with two identical series cells, both the y-intercept and the magnitude of the gradient double. Editorial worked explanation: For a cell, V=ε−Ir. Extrapolating the line to I=0 gives ε=1.50 V. Using two points, for example (0.20 A,1.35 V) and (1.40 A,0.45 V), the gradient is (0.45−1.35)/(1.40−0.20)=−0.75 V A⁻¹, hence r=0.75 Ω. Two cells in series have total emf 3.00 V and total internal resistance 1.50 Ω, so V=3.00−1.50I: the intercept and negative gradient magnitude double. The x-intercept remains ε/r=2.0 A.
answer.evidence: Pearson Edexcel WPH12_01_2306_MS checked on PDF page 7; visible worked explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The supplied series circuit contains a fixed resistor and a light-dependent resistor (LDR) connected to a cell. Explain why the total power dissipated by the circuit changes as the light intensity incident on the LDR increases. Include why the LDR resistance changes.

answer.text: Official markscheme conclusion: the total power increases. Editorial worked explanation: Greater light intensity provides energy that makes more charge carriers mobile in the LDR, increasing the number density of conduction electrons and lowering the LDR’s resistance. The total series resistance therefore decreases. The cell emf remains fixed, so the circuit current increases. For the whole circuit, P=VI=εI (or P=ε²/R_total), hence the increased current and reduced total resistance mean greater total power dissipation.
answer.evidence: Pearson Edexcel WPH12_01_2306_MS checked on PDF page 9; visible worked explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The supplied graph shows current I against potential difference V for one car headlight. (a) Determine the minimum V for at least 35 W. (b)(i) Explain advantages of connecting two headlights in parallel rather than series across a 12.0 V battery. (b)(ii) Use graph data to test the claim that the parallel pair’s combined resistance is one quarter of the series pair’s combined resistance.

answer.text: Official markscheme results: minimum V=9.0 V; parallel connection is brighter and independently reliable; the resistance ratio is about 2.9, so the factor-of-four claim is false. Editorial worked explanation: At V=9.0 V, the graph gives I≈3.9 A and VI≈35.1 W, the first point reaching 35 W. In parallel, each lamp receives 12.0 V, gives greater power/brightness, and one remains lit if the other fails; in series each receives about 6 V and either break opens the circuit. From the graph, at 12.0 V one lamp draws 4.6 A, so R_lamp=12.0/4.6=2.61 Ω and R_parallel=2.61/2=1.30 Ω. At 6.0 V one lamp draws 3.2 A, so R_lamp=6.0/3.2=1.88 Ω and R_series=2(1.88)=3.76 Ω. The ratio 3.76/1.30=2.9, not 4, because the filament is non-ohmic and its resistance changes with operating temperature.
answer.evidence: Pearson Edexcel WPH12_01_2306_MS checked on PDF page 11; visible worked explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A conducting wire has constant cross-sectional area A and constant temperature. A graph of resistance R against length L is plotted. Which expression equals its gradient? A. resistivity  B. resistivity×A  C. resistivity/A  D. A/resistivity

answer.text: Official answer C. Editorial worked explanation: R=ρL/A. With ρ and A constant, R=(ρ/A)L, so the gradient ΔR/ΔL is ρ/A.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 9; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Two identical 3.0 V cells, each of internal resistance r, are in series with a 145 Ω resistor. The current is 0.040 A. What is r? A. 0.10 Ω  B. 0.20 Ω  C. 2.5 Ω  D. 5.0 Ω

answer.text: Official answer C. Editorial worked explanation: Total emf is 6.0 V, so total circuit resistance is 6.0/0.040=150 Ω. The two cells together contribute 150−145=5.0 Ω, hence each has r=2.5 Ω.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 9; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Two copper wires X and Y are in series and have equal length; X has the larger cross-sectional area. Which two quantities are equal in both? A. charge-carrier density and current  B. charge-carrier density and drift velocity  C. current and resistance  D. drift velocity and resistance

answer.text: Official answer A. Editorial worked explanation: Both wires are copper, so their charge-carrier density n is the same. Series components carry the same current I. From the supplied model v=I/(nqA), the larger area of X makes its drift speed smaller, and R=ρL/A makes its resistance smaller, so neither drift speed nor resistance is equal.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 9; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.given_text: Use I=nqAv, where n is charge-carrier number density, q is carrier charge magnitude, A is cross-sectional area and v is drift speed.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: How do resistance and resistivity change when the length of a conductor is increased while its material, temperature and cross-sectional area are unchanged? A. both constant  B. resistance constant, resistivity increases  C. resistance increases, resistivity constant  D. both increase

answer.text: Official answer C. Editorial worked explanation: R=ρL/A, so increasing L with A fixed increases R. Resistivity ρ is a material property and remains constant because the material and temperature are unchanged.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 9; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A tungsten lamp is in series with a variable resistor, and a voltmeter is across the lamp. The resistor is adjusted so the filament temperature increases. What happens? A. lamp resistance and voltmeter reading decrease  B. resistance decreases, reading increases  C. resistance increases, reading decreases  D. both increase

answer.text: Official answer D. Editorial worked explanation: A hotter tungsten filament has greater resistivity and resistance. In the potential divider, V_lamp=εR_lamp/(R_lamp+R_variable); the adjustment that raises filament temperature and current gives a larger share of the supply voltage across the lamp. Thus both resistance and voltmeter reading increase.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 9; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: At a circuit junction, currents 0.5 A and I enter while currents 1.6 A and 1.4 A leave. What is I? A. 0.3 A  B. 0.5 A  C. 2.5 A  D. 3.0 A

answer.text: Official answer C. Editorial worked explanation: Charge conservation gives total current in=total current out: 0.5+I=1.6+1.4. Therefore I=3.0−0.5=2.5 A.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 9; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: In the supplied light-meter circuit, an electron moves through a potential difference of 3.0 V from the metal plate to the electrode. Calculate the work done on it.

answer.text: Official markscheme result: 4.8×10⁻¹⁹ J. Editorial worked explanation: The magnitude of work is W=qV=(1.60×10⁻¹⁹)(3.0)=4.8×10⁻¹⁹ J. The electric field transfers this energy to the electron.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 14; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A four-terminal box is connected to a cell and two ammeters as shown; X is the top-left terminal. Each option A–D shows equal-resistance connections placed in the box. Which option gives the same reading on both ammeters?

answer.text:
Published key D checked; editorial worked explanation:

D. In D there is one complete path: current enters X through the left ammeter, crosses the top resistor, passes through the right ammeter, and returns along the lower wire. The same series current therefore passes through both ammeters. The other networks either split current or provide a short path, so the right ammeter does not carry the complete cell current.

evidence.detail: AQA 7408/1 June 2023 published key D, mark-scheme PDF page 27; explanation independently authored and checked.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A resistor dissipates 100 W across a 25 V supply with negligible internal resistance. The supply is reduced to 20 V and the resistor is replaced so the power remains 100 W. What is the percentage decrease in resistance?

A. 20%
B. 36%
C. 64%
D. 80%

answer.text:
Published key B checked; editorial worked explanation:

B. With fixed power, R=V²/P. Initially R₁=25²/100=6.25 Ω; finally R₂=20²/100=4.00 Ω. The percentage decrease is (6.25−4.00)/6.25×100%=36%.

evidence.detail: AQA 7408/1 June 2023 published key B, mark-scheme PDF page 28; explanation independently authored and checked.
